t: You're at the Royal Hospital Chelsea, a retirement home for around 300 veterans of the British Army. King Charles the Second founded it in 1682 as an almshouse, which is the old meaning of hospital. It stands on a 66-acre site and is an independent charity. Margaret Thatcher and her husband Denis are buried here. So are Hannah Snell and Christian Davies, two women who disguised themselves as men to serve in the army. Christian Davies later lived here as a Chelsea Pensioner, and Daniel Defoe turned her story into a book. Field Marshal Sir George White, a Victoria Cross winner, died here.
